title: Faulty cable caused Lisbon funicular crash, inquiry finds
summary: Report says snapped cable between cabins was substandard and city’s other funiculars should fix risk before reopening The funicular that crashed in Lisbon killing 16 people in early September had a faulty cable, the official inquiry said on Monday as it recommended the city’s vehicles stay out of service until their safety can be confirmed. The accident, which saw the picture-postcard 19th-century Elevador da Glória hurtle into a building after careering off the rails, shocked the Portuguese capital and laid bare fears over the safety of the popular yet ageing tourist attraction.
